results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. For further information, VFB holds a range of data on the mushroom body, including images, neuron records, and lineage clones. Specifically, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body") tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells, including gamma Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are several types of Kenyon cells, including KCab-c(i), KCab-c, KCg-m, Kenyon cell of main calyx, and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. Specifically, VFB holds [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100247,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") records for subclasses of gamma Kenyon cells, which include [larval [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain")](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049827 "Open larval gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049830 "Open KCg-s in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-s4](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049832 "Open KCg-s4 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-t](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049833 "Open KCg-t in Virtual Fly Brain"), [KCg-d](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110932 "Open KCg-d in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCg-m, KCg-s1, KCg-s2, KCg, and KCg-s3. Additionally, VFB has annotated data on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, splits targeting gamma Kenyon cells, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, downstream connectivity classes, and upstream connectivity classes, which can be queried for further information.

results.title: Basic connectivity

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. According to VFB, it has a unique anatomy and connectivity, with its large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle. The giant fiber neuron descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus and has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. 

In terms of connectivity, the giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend. VFB holds [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of downstream connectivity classes and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of upstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron, which can be used to further explore its connectivity. 

VFB also provides information on available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron, including several GAL4 and p65 expression patterns. Relevant publications listed in VFB include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, and others, which can be consulted for more detailed information on the giant fiber neuron's anatomy, connectivity, and function. 

Additionally, VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the DNp01 neuron, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, which can be used to visualize and study the giant fiber neuron in more detail.
